title: [SOLVED+ Tutorial ] Problem with giving events more than 3 frames of animation

posts.author: NoClue
posts.body:
Hello everyone, I'm working on a project and it's going fairly well, I've been having a lot of fun despite some difficulties in using the larger character sprite sheets from PVGames, but so far I've got them all sorted out but for one issue. I can't seem to figure out how to make the events representing the enemies use more than 3 frames of animation.
These are the sprites I'm using for a Timber Wolf enemy. I have two separate spritesheets because when the player is detected by a randomly roaming enemy, its behaviour changes along with its sprite, and it begins to chase. I was also using QSprite, which is why the file names are the way they are. If I use something like Galv character frames it gets cut off, here's what that looks like:
Before anyone asks, I did select the upper-left part in the viewer inside RPG Maker MV itself, the same issue is there.
QSprite doesn't seem to work on events (the sprites are still working properly but only for the first three frames, if I make the main character the sprite sheet, it works perfectly, so I know the sprite sheet isn't the problem). Galv cuts off the sprites, and I feel like if I knew how to change the dimensions for that I could set it so that it uses the larger sprite correctly, but I'm stumped on where to find documentation for how to do that. If anyone had any other plugins they'd like to suggest, I would be happy to take their suggestions, but it seems hard in general to get events to use more than three frames if the sprites you're using are larger than the typical sprites.
I also am handling the detection with a separate parallel event. I'm not sure if that makes a difference, I kind of doubt it, however I did so in order to have both a randomly roaming enemy behaviour followed by a charge when the player is discovered. If I simply knew what to do to use more frames with events, I feel like I would be happy with it.

I solved it! I also figured out my problem with Galv Character Animations, and it was actually the notes feature and idle animations that were the core culprits. So I'm going to give an impromtpu tutorial for everyone who might want to use more sprites and has my same issue.
So to start off, you were right about the size issue. If you're using Galv's plugins, you must always take the size of your sprites, then multiply their width by 32, and height by 8 (because Galv uses 32 frames by 8 frames for their plugin, I was initially unaware of this). This gives the sprite sheet needed, and that's why you suggested that size.
Now the part that was really tripping me up, is that Galv Character Animations NEED idle animations, or at least an empty slot for them. There's no ifs, ands or buts about it, the first 8 columns you have MUST be dedicated to idle animations. These can just be a static image of a sprite repeated 8 times, or leave it blank so that they're invisible when still, that doesn't matter. What does matter is if you don't do this, it won't work right.
Also keep in mind that the first 8 columns will always be the idle animations and directions, the second 8 will always be the walking animations and directions, and the third 8 columns will always be running animations. The rest doesn't matter, because I'm not using jumping animations, so they can be blank. The directions your sprites must face in the following rows are as follows:
Row 1: Up
Row 2: Left
Row 3: Right
Row 4: Down
Row 5: Down Right
Row 6: Down Left
Row 7: Up Right
Row 8: Up Left
If you do not have them facing these directions, their movements will not match their sprites. You might need to re-order PVGames' sprites, or follow Mathmaster74's code change because of this, since the diagonal sprites do not follow these directions by default. If you wish to change the code, open up GALV_DiagonalMovement plugin, and do the following:
Find this:
Galv.DM.diagRow = {
3: 0,
1: 1,
9: 2,
7: 3
};
Replace it with this:
So that instead they are as follows:
Galv.DM.diagRow = {
3: 2,
1: 0,
9: 3,
7: 1
};
Then it will work. Now:
I started a new project, here's the plugin order.
You need to add <charAnims> in the notes for it to properly recognise the sprite sheet. I didn't even realise that was there for a while, so that also tripped me up. Without this, the events will refuse to recognise the sprite sheet no matter how you label or remake the sprite. This was what really tripped me up, and in my inexperience I didn't know what the documentation wanted me to do with the note script.
Make sure everything is labeled correctly, and as a bonus, I'm also going to go over how to do a chase with a random enemy.
This is a random enemy that when it touches the player, starts a battle. It moves around the map randomly, and there's nothing special about it otherwise. In the top left of the map however, is this event:
This event runs parallel (that's important) and it uses Galv Event Detectors with the following settings:
When a player gets within a certain range of the wolf, the condition WolfDetected is flipped, and the Wolf event changes to page 2, and the parallel event also changes to page 2. Page 2 of the parallel event is just a blank page to turn it off, however for the Wolf, the page is the following:
This is literally the same script as the first page, except I swapped the running and walking animations on the sprite sheet to give it the appearance it's running. You can also turn up the speed to help with that. To chase the player I used the following custom move route script:
This causes the wolf to follow the behaviour, specifically Behaviour 1 (not Behaviour 0) in Galv Event Detectors:
Finally, we need a way to turn off the WolfDetected Condition, but I set that so it happens if the player runs away, and you can also tag it to the exits of a map, or safe places you want the player to hide. Here's what it looks like attached to the fleeing script you learn in MV's tutorial:
For whatever reason I could not find a good tutorial on having random enemies detect the player then chase them, so I'm making my own in case/for when I forget how to do this in a few years, assuming I fall out of practice.
Lastly, when enemies swap sprites like that, there's a noticeable jitter, so to fix that get these two plugins:
SRD Game Upgrade is required for SRD PreloaderCore, so now open preloader core, and choose to load the images in advance. For my purpose I simply chose all because I'm not using many character images at the moment.
And that's how you use both the full list of the character sprites for events, and how you do a chase from a random behaviour with little script knowledge. As for how the player moves, that follows similar conventions, or you can use QSprite to handle that part. That one is very easy to use and learn, and there's plenty of tutorials that make it simple. This was a lot harder to figure out so that's why I went into detail.
Here's links to everything I mentioned that would be needed, since I also hate searching for plugins that people tell others to get without providing links themselves:
Galv Character Frames:
https://galvs-scripts.com/2015/12/12/mv-character-frames/
Galv Diagonal Movement:
https://galvs-scripts.com/2015/12/12/mv-diagonal-movement/
Galv Character Animations:
https://galvs-scripts.com/2015/11/03/mv-character-animations/
Game Upgrade:
http://sumrndm.site/game-upgrade/
Preloader Core:
http://sumrndm.site/preloader-core/
Also, here's Mathmaster74's tutorial:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1lYFLIZ-lZpS5kRmSCqVptr6oA4IfSEAoGXk3YE8zkOM/edit?tab=t.0
I really wish they'd explain why you are doing the things they ask, because without being given a reason, I have a hard time knowing what the effect is, or what is going wrong if something does go wrong.
Thanks again for the assistance.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Basically what you originally ignored was that PVG's sprites add TWO new functions to the sprites - more frames AND diagonal movement.
So only adding a plugin for 8 frames alone didn't work, that was why you had 2 sprites for a while - the engine didn't know what to  do with the additional rows for diagonal movement.
there are other solutions possible, not only the one above, but you would always have to have plugins for combined diagonal movement and more frame sprites.
